title: Predictive experimental selection of a chosen crystal form

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to specify a desired crystal form in advance and predict experimental conditions that reproducibly favor its formation. It would connect a quantitative account of nucleation and early growth to practical control of the crystallization experiment. Success would mean reliable statistical selectivity across repeated experiments, rather than certainty about every individual nucleus. The intended scope extends across organic molecules, inorganic frameworks, and macromolecules; that breadth is an ambition, not a demonstrated capability.

The central task is to control which structure forms, including cases where the desired structure is metastable. Predicting relative stability alone does not establish how to reach that structure experimentally: cluster dynamics, growth rates, and the route to crystallization can affect the outcome. The supplied account of colloidal polymorph control illustrates this distinction within a particular model system.

Scope clarification: polymorphs share a chemical composition but have different crystal structures. Salts and hydrates expand the possible solid-form targets through changes in composition and should therefore be identified separately. A selection framework could address all these targets, but its predictions would need to specify both the intended composition and structure.

significance.text: If demonstrated across the intended material classes, this capability would turn crystallization knowledge into prospective experimental control. Within its validated domain, a researcher could request a particular form and use predicted conditions to obtain it reproducibly. Screening would remain useful for discovering forms and developing models; the additional advance would be successful prediction before the validation experiment, without searching conditions until the target happens to appear.

Conditional downstream benefits include reliable access to metastable forms, recovery of documented disappearing or difficult-to-reproduce forms, and access to forms missed by previous screens. These benefits require more than initiating the desired structure: the form must persist long enough to be measured and used. Reproducibility at manufacturing scale would require separate validation because laboratory selection alone does not establish control during scale-up.

The scientific motivation is that crystallization pathways can materially change kinetics and outcomes, while the reported colloidal experiments connect polymorph formation to dynamics and growth as well as stability. These observations make predictive selection consequential, but they do not establish transfer from colloidal particles to molecular crystals, frameworks, or macromolecules. Its revolutionary significance is therefore a conditional judgment about the proposed breadth, not a claim that existing model-system control already delivers it.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is a transferable relationship between experimental conditions, nucleation and early-growth behavior, and the probability of obtaining a specified form. Such a framework would need to predict which pathways matter in a given system and translate that prediction into controllable experimental choices. The supplied 2024 review supports the importance of non-classical crystallization pathways and the challenges of elucidating them, but its available abstract does not establish the full mechanism-by-mechanism account needed for this framework.

Mechanistic questions retained from the research include how routes involving dense liquids, amorphous particles, or particle attachment affect selection, and when one route dominates another. These are candidate mechanisms for the proposed framework to resolve, rather than a verified assertion that all such routes compete in every material class. The supplied review preview is insufficient to substantiate their detailed scope or universal applicability.

Proposed engineering requirements include predicting outcome probabilities rather than a single favored structure, distinguishing initial formation from subsequent transformation, and identifying conditions that preserve a desired metastable form until the relevant measurement or use. Transfer across material classes would also require showing when the same predictive principles apply and when additional system-specific information is necessary. These requirements follow from the intended capability; they are not established performance specifications.

Whether a fully general theory is possible remains uncertain. Broad, explicitly bounded transfer could still constitute the intended breakthrough without a universal law. The supplied evidence neither proves that universality is impossible nor establishes the absence of a transferable framework as of 1 November 2026.

current_state.text: The review by Du, Bae, and De Yoreo, published in Nature Reviews Materials on 6 February 2024, describes non-classical crystallization pathways in soft and organic materials and states that they can substantially affect crystallization kinetics and outcomes. It identifies unresolved pathway questions and opportunities for material design. According to the supplied evidence review, the retained document is a subscription preview: extraction was not truncated, but the article body and detailed figures were unavailable for assessment. The abstract therefore supports the broad motivation, not all the detailed pathway claims in the earlier research.

A Tohoku University release dated 22 April 2025 describes a study published in Communications Physics on 9 April 2025 using heteroepitaxial experiments with polystyrene colloidal particles. The release reports that polymorph probabilities depended on size and stability and that particle additives controlled polymorph formation. It also connects the outcomes to cluster dynamics and growth rates. This documents a dated, system-specific advance in controlling crystal form; the supplied material provides no numerical selectivity or independent replication result.

The complete retained source for that result is the university news release, which identifies and links the peer-reviewed study. The research paper itself was not supplied for assessment. The release supports the reported colloidal result, while leaving its detailed experimental performance and transfer to molecular crystals or industrial processes unassessed.

The earlier research attributes to the 2024 seventh crystal-structure-prediction blind-test report an argument that nucleation, growth, and transformation rates are needed because energy landscapes predict more forms than are observed. It also characterizes a 30 July 2024 Organic Process Research & Development review as discussing industrial nucleation tools that improve seed consistency. Neither source has a retained document in the supplied source index, so these attributions could not be checked against source content in the supplied review. They remain potentially relevant context, rather than established findings of this record; the missing documents do not show that the claims are false.

Taken together, the supplied evidence documents pathway research and limited experimental control. It does not demonstrate the proposed breadth of predictive selection. Because no bounded freshness search was supplied, it also does not establish whether a broader capability remained unavailable as of 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed benchmark: before validation experiments, specify the target form and predicted conditions for at least ten chemically diverse targets spanning the claimed material classes. Include at least two metastable forms and one documented disappearing or hard-to-reproduce form. An independent laboratory should then obtain the specified form as the majority product across preregistered replicate trials. The target counts and inclusion requirements are proposed tests of breadth, not published consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed benchmark

completion_criteria.text: The protocol should define how phase fraction is measured, when it is measured, what constitutes majority product, how many replicates are required, and what success-rate threshold counts as reliable selection. For metastable targets, it should distinguish successful initial formation from persistence over a predefined interval. Conditions and permitted adjustments should be fixed before validation; searching until the desired form appears would not establish prospective predictive performance.

related_concepts.text: CRX-03, “Chemical-accuracy prediction of which molecular crystal will form,” overlaps through prediction of crystal outcomes. The proposed distinction is that CRX-07 requires experimental conditions that select a requested form, potentially including a kinetically disfavored metastable form. Stability ranking can inform that task, but does not by itself provide experimental access. The supplied roster gives only CRX-03’s title, so it should not be assumed that its complete scope is limited to thermodynamic ranking.

CRX-11, “Diffraction-quality crystals of arbitrary macromolecules on demand,” overlaps when the targets are macromolecules. Its title emphasizes obtaining suitable crystals; CRX-07 emphasizes selecting which form results. Producing a first diffraction-quality crystal and reproducibly selecting a specified form are distinct achievements, even when the same experiment contributes to both.

CRX-13, “A growth rulebook that suppresses defects, twins, and disorder in arbitrary crystals,” overlaps through control of growth. The proposed boundary is between selecting a crystal form and controlling defects or disorder within that form. A selected form can still have poor crystal quality, and defect suppression alone does not establish selection among competing forms. These distinctions use the supplied titles and research framing; detailed definitions of the neighboring concepts were not supplied.

unresolved_issues: Whether a broadly transferable predictive selection capability existed as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because no bounded freshness search was supplied.
The detailed mechanisms and material-class coverage of the 2024 Nature review remain unassessed beyond its available preview.
The quantitative performance, experimental limitations, and independent reproducibility of the 2025 colloidal study require assessment of the underlying paper and additional evidence.
The specific seventh blind-test and industrial-nucleation-review attributions remain unverified because their source documents were not retained.
The proposed benchmark still requires numerical choices for replicate count, success probability, measurement protocol, and persistence interval.
The feasibility of transfer across organic molecules, inorganic frameworks, and macromolecules, and the possibility of a fully general theory, remain open.
Detailed boundaries with CRX-03, CRX-11, and CRX-13 remain provisional because their full concept records were not supplied.
